board_removal_steps: Switch off and unplug the 12 V input and both output wire pairs at the board terminals (wires are not part of the mount).
With a 2.5 mm hex key straight down from above, undo the four M3x6 screws (the key column above each head is clear to 45 mm).
Lift the board straight up 20 mm: nothing is above it, nothing touches it but the four pad tops.
Swap the board. To fit: set it on the four pads, start the four M3 screws by hand, snug by feel. The mount stays on the rail throughout (its 2 M5 screws are not touched).

D2.fit_reasoning: The printer holds +-0.15 mm, so a line-to-line Ø52 seat cannot be shown to clamp: the bore prints 51.85..52.15 against a ring of 52.0 (-0.013). Each half stands back 0.15 mm from the split plane, so before tightening the halves are 0.30 mm apart; the screws draw them together and the bore across Y becomes bore - 0.30 = 51.55..51.85, always under the ring: 0.14 to 0.45 mm of diametral interference, taken up by the PETG halves (E 1.9 GPa against 210 for steel), not by the ring. The gap does not close once the ring is clamped: the ring stops the halves, so the clamp comes from the closing travel (0.30 mm minus what the ring takes), not from print tolerance; the screws only need to pull until the ring bites. (The FEA twin is the split-CLOSED state, see why.) Seat width 7.3 for the 7.0 bearing leaves 0.3 mm of axial play, so a -0.15 print cannot pinch it axially; the shoulders (opening Ø46) back the outer ring end faces (r 24..26 against a lip from r 23) and clear the turning inner ring (r 22) by 1.0 mm radially, checked with 6,000 sampled points of the inner ring volume and a sweep with 0.5 mm margin: 0 inside the housings. Printed on its split face (Y up) the seat is an open trough with no overhang.

clearances_mm.outer_ring_end_face_backed_by_lip: lip from r 23, face r 24..26 (2 mm of land, 1 mm of lip over the seal gap)

screw_load_n.note: tension = plane-fitted stress over the shank section at three heights times its area. +Y: 91-95 N each against 75 by hand (+21 to +27 %). Balance for the upper half: screw tension = ring push + split compression. Sections just above and below the split read -69 N (compression, +Y), so 371 = 300 + 71: the extra is prying, which exists in the split-CLOSED twin only. +X: tension 132 N, split compression -109 to -112 N, so the ring pushes the upper half up with about 22 N (5.5 N per screw): the first hand estimate (23.9 each from F/pi) did not hold; the screws mostly carry prying from the upper half sliding 0.2 mm in X on the frictionless split. I dropped the F tan 21 argument. Preload is not modelled; head bearing limit 17.4 mm2 x 22.5/2 = 196 N per screw, so snug preload must stay under about 100 N per screw on top of 95 N service.

D2.how_bodies_were_held: Lower half: face Y -32 fixed. Upper half: four steel pins (Ø3.0 shank in the Ø3.4 holes, head bonded on the counterbore floor, Ø4.0 end bonded in the insert hole) and no-penetration contact on both patches of the split face (each half has two, X < -23 and X > 23). Ring (Ø51.9 x 7, 0.05 mm radial clearance, 0.4 mm chamfers): four soft pads (E 0.5 MPa, Ø1.8 x 1.0) bonded between its end face and the floors of four 0.85 mm recesses in the shoulders; they carry 0.17 to 0.19 N of the 300 N (0.06 %, from their own shear and stretch). The load is a bearing load on the ring bore.
D2.contact_proof: Against a bonded twin, same mesh (74,551 nodes): +Y ring movement 0.140 mm against 0.0111 bonded (12.6 times), largest displacement 0.232 against 0.0348 (6.7 times), screws +91..95 N each against -14 N (unloaded) bonded; the unloaded lower seat opens 0.126..0.140 mm at every angle from -180 to -30 degrees while the loaded upper arc is closed (0.000 from 0 to 150). +X: movement 0.177 against 0.032 (5.5 times), screws 132 N against 36 N, the -X side opens 0.20 mm. Reaction 300.0 N in both. An independent section force through the lower half reads 295 N (-1.7 %) for +Y. A section just below the split reads -68 N: the prying force at the split faces.
D2.governing: lower half, +X case: shear between layers 2.87 MPa (printed split face up, factor 4.6); the same half has von Mises 7.07 MPa (6.4) and layer tension 3.79 MPa (5.9). Counting the nodes at the seat edge where it meets the split face (a contact edge) the peak is 9.4 MPa von Mises, factor 4.8

print_orientation.housing_upper: split face up, outer face Y +32 on the bed (layers stacked along Y): the seat is an open trough, counterbores and screw holes are vertical, no supports. Lowest factor 4.58 against 3.77 and 3.82 for the other two directions
print_orientation.housing_lower: split face up, mounting face Y -32 on the bed (layers along Y): the M4 insert holes open on the bed face and are filled from the mounting face; the insert holes at the split face are vertical

D2.why: Reaction 300.0 N in every solve; contact proved against the bonded twin; both patches of each split face are in the set (the first runs had one patch and were wrong: tags a and c, INVALID); pads carry 0.06 %; section check 295 N; hand screw loads differ by 21-27 % (+Y) and 16 % (+X) and the difference is accounted for by prying and the contact angle (section force below the split). Verdict margin, not converged: one entry (upper half +X layer tension, 2.26, 1.94, 1.28 MPa) falls 34 % at the last step. Valid for a snug joint in the split-closed state: no preload modelled Twin differs from the saved parts: split faces closed (saved halves have 0.15 mm relief each), ring Ø51.9 with 0.4 chamfers (saved ring Ø52), four 0.85 mm pad recesses, steel pins in place of M3 screws and inserts, no friction. Hidden zones read separately: counterbore walls and ribs 6.2-7.2 MPa von Mises, insert surrounds 2.9-7.2.
D2.sf_layer_note: lowest layer-tension factor: 7.2 MPa across layers (layers along Y) at the counterbore floor corner, stable over three meshes (6.6, 7.2, 7.1); 2.7 MPa at 0.5 mm from the wall (factor 8.3), about 1 MPa from 1 mm: a corner, reported at its value. Elsewhere layer tension is 3.8 MPa (factor 5.9)
D2.notes: Runs tagged a and c are INVALID (one patch of each split face in the contact set; the other bonded). Valid runs are tag d on pair_fe2. sf_layer uses the counterbore corner.
